compiled_state.title: RED: shell-level entry-point test — process_events with multi-commit tracker directory
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Testing Mode
RED

## What
Write a failing test that drives bridge-outbound.py (or process_events) at the entry-point level with a multi-commit git fixture to catch shell-level diff-window regressions. Required by done definition #7.

## Why
The original HEAD~1..HEAD bug lived in the shell git diff invocation in process_events, not in Python logic. Unit tests that import _outbound_cursor directly do not catch regressions in the git invocation string or argument order. At least one test must exercise the actual subprocess call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Test file: tests/scripts/test_bridge_outbound.py (add new test function)
- Test name: test_process_events_multi_commit_catches_all_events
- Setup: create a temporary git repo at tmp_path with .tickets-tracker/ structure; make 4 commits each adding one event file (tickets T1–T4); set .outbound-checkpoint.json to the SHA of the first commit
- Call: process_events(tickets_dir=str(tmp_path / '.tickets-tracker'), acli_client=mock_acli, git_diff_output=None) — letting process_events run its internal git commands
- Assert: all 4 event files are parsed (mock_acli.create_issue called at least once per CREATE event, or events list contains all 4 tickets)
- This test MUST FAIL before the cursor implementation (currently process_events uses HEAD~1..HEAD and would miss commits 1-3)

Alternative if subprocess approach is impractical in pytest: test may use importlib to load bridge-outbound and call process_events with a git fixture (tmp git repo), calling the git subprocess internally.

## Files to Modify
- tests/scripts/test_bridge_outbound.py

comments.body:
AC-AMENDMENT (gap-analysis):
1. Off-by-one: 'cursor at commit-1 SHA' means checkpoint records the SHA of commit 1. On next run, we process commit-1..HEAD = commits 2, 3, 4 (3 events). To observe all 4 events, checkpoint must be at the empty-tree / initial commit (before any event commits). Use cursor=None (cold-start path) OR set cursor to the SHA of a 'setup' commit that precedes the 4 event commits.
2. Entry-point invocation: import bridge_outbound via importlib.util (matching existing test patterns for bridge scripts), then call process_events() directly. The test exercises the git subprocess call internally — this catches shell-level diff-window regressions even in pytest.
